question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's consolidated authority within the Chinese Communist Party, backed by extensive personnel appointments, military purges, and institutional controls, underpins trader expectations that he will retain his roles as general secretary, president, and Central Military Commission chairman through the end of 2026. With the 21st Party Congress scheduled for late 2027 and no designated successor or internal challenges emerging, analyses point to a likely fourth term beginning then rather than any near-term exit. Recent developments, including ongoing elite reshuffles and limited public signals of transition, reinforce this positioning. While the 95.5% implied probability for continuation reflects broad consensus on structural barriers to removal, low-probability disruptions such as acute health developments, elite fractures, or unforeseen policy crises could still shift outcomes before the market resolves on December 31, 2026.
